language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

Q2 included a $77M after-tax Corporate charge for legacy mass tort, and Q2 2025 had an $88M one. In Q3 2025 the Corporate core loss was only $25M and core EPS was $1.50. Seasonally, Q3 has no such charge, so stripping out about $50M of Corporate drag alone is worth about +$0.18/share against a bar set at Q2's level.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Higher fixed-income NII was cited as a driver of the Q3 2025 beat, which sold off -1.12%. NII has not moved this stock alone.

findings.finding: Peer workers'-comp deterioration. Hartford's Middle & Large Business underlying combined ratio rose to 99.5 in Q3 2026 from 91.4 a year earlier (91.3 in Q1, 95.3 in Q2), driven mainly by a higher workers'-comp loss ratio. NCCI puts the industry's 2025 accident-year workers'-comp combined ratio at 102 against 91 calendar-year, with releases bridging the gap. CNA's Commercial segment (middle market and national accounts) writes workers' comp with rates down low single digits, and Q2 favorable development came partly from workers' comp. Commercial's underlying ratio was already 92.8 against 90.6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Underlying deterioration plus adverse development drove the Q1 2026 print to -7.95%. Q2's 2.5-point underlying deterioration came with a beat and the stock rose +2.13%.

findings.finding: Peer catastrophe losses rose year on year in Q3 2026, mainly from US severe convective storms. Travelers was at $538M against $302M, Chubb at $705M against $285M and W.R. Berkley at $85.9M against $78.5M; Hartford fell to $106M from $389M. Gallagher Re puts US SCS insured losses at $43B or more through Q3, alongside Hawaii hurricane impacts. CNA's Q3 2025 cat load was low at 1.5 points of combined ratio, so a year-on-year headwind is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lower cats helped the Q3 2025 beat, which still went -1.12%. Cats were 3.6 points in Q1 2026 (-7.95%, though reserves led that move) and 2.3 points in Q2 2026 (+2.13%).

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 peer reserve tone in commercial lines was benign. Travelers' Business Insurance had $41M of favorable prior-year development from 'better than expected loss experience in all major product lines' (excluding a $295M asbestos addition), against $125M unfavorable in Q3 2025. Selective had no net unfavorable development, against 3.7 points adverse a year earlier. Cincinnati Financial released $94M. Adverse development in excess casualty and professional lines is what sank CNA's Q1 2026 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior-year development is the line this stock has punished: Q1 2026 had 4.1 points of adverse development and fell -7.95%. Q2 2026 had zero P&C development and rose +2.13%.

findings.finding: Q3 is when CNA runs its annual Life & Group reserve review (long-term care morbidity, cost-of-care inflation and structured settlements). Last year it cost $7M pretax for LTC and $2M for structured settlements, essentially neutral, with statutory LTC margin at $1.5B. Q2 2026 Life & Group swung to a $10M core loss from $1M of income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two reviews (2024: $15M pretax, 2025: $7M) were immaterial and did not visibly move the stock (Q3 2025: -1.12%).

The P&C underlying combined ratio was 94.5 in Q1 2026 and 94.2 in Q2, against 92.1 and 91.7 a year earlier, and Q3 2025's comparable was 91.3. P&C rate was flat in Q2 and International rate was -5%. findings.finding: Peer and industry read-through says CHH's Q3 US RevPAR probably beats its own framing ('above Q2's +1.3%'). Wyndham, the closest economy/midscale franchisor, printed Q3 2026 US RevPAR +6% on 2026-10-21 against -5% in Q3 2025 (two-year stack about +0.7%). CHH's Q3 2025 comparison was -3.2%, so the same two-year stack implies roughly +4% for CHH. Hilton printed US RevPAR +7%. STR's industry series ran July +8.2%, August +2.0%, and +10.4% and +14.2% in the last two September weeks. The offset: CHH said the World Cup gave it only 'limited' Q3 exposure, while Wyndham credited a favorable World Cup impact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): US RevPAR +1.3% with a raised RevPAR/EBITDA guide bought +2.93%. Q3 2025 (US RevPAR -3.2%, guide cut) still bought +5.98%. Q1 2026, an adj EPS miss with a steady outlook, fell -15.58%. The stock reacts to EPS and guidance more than to RevPAR.

findings.finding: The Street already models a guidance raise. FY26 consensus adj EPS of $7.14 sits above the top of the company's $6.86-7.10 range, which was lowered on 2026-08-05 for higher interest expense and a 26% tax rate. A RevPAR raise that leaves EPS guidance at or near $7.10 would read as a miss against the bar. Hilton also flagged Q4 headwinds (US midterm elections, the Middle East), while Wyndham guided Q4 US RevPAR in line with Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: RevPAR/EBITDA guide raised but EPS guide trimmed, stock +2.93%. 2025-11-05: guide cut, stock +5.98% (bar was low). 2026-04-30: EPS miss with a steady outlook, -15.58%. The direction of EPS guidance against the bar decides the large moves.

findings.finding: This peer group sold its Q3 RevPAR beats. Wyndham printed US RevPAR +6% and raised its FY RevPAR guide after the close on 2026-10-21, then fell 4.2% (78.36 to 75.07) on Oct 22 and 3.5% on Oct 23, with adj EPS down 2% on a marketing-fund timing swing. Hilton printed US +7% and raised its RevPAR guide on 2026-10-27, and fell about 5% premarket on a revenue miss. CHH fell 1.5% and 3.1% in sympathy on Oct 22-23 (113.66 to 108.48), then recovered to about $112.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHH's own record: +2.93% on an RevPAR acceleration and raise (Aug 2026) and -15.58% on an EPS miss (Apr 2026). EPS quality, not RevPAR, has driven the large moves.

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 6.33M shares short (2026-10-15 settlement), 12.8 days to cover against roughly 0.49M average daily volume, about 14% of shares outstanding and more of the family-reduced float. If the US RevPAR and guidance raise the peers point to arrive with a clean EPS beat, short covering is a mechanism for an outsized upside move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last seven reactions were +5.98% and +2.93% on raised or better-than-feared outlooks. The baseline does not record short interest at those dates.

findings.finding: The Q3 2025 comparison includes about $9.5M of liquidated damages (in other revenue) that will not recur, roughly $0.15 of adj EPS after tax on about 45M shares. Consensus $2.26 still asks for about +8% growth over last year's $2.10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable. The item was flagged by the company on the Q2 call.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-28 CHH signed a $500M senior unsecured term loan (SOFR+1.25%, maturing 2029-08-28, Wells Fargo agent) for general purposes including debt repayment. Net leverage was 3.1x at Q2, inside the 3-4x target, and the 2026 buyback is guided at $175-225M ($133M done by July 31). This is refinancing and capital-return capacity, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed. Higher interest expense was one reason the EPS guide was trimmed on 2026-08-05.

outside_window.finding: The first disposition of wholly owned hotels (19 operating) is expected in H1 2027, subject to market conditions. It is a capital-recycling catalyst, but not in this window unless announced with the print.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): RevPAR read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.7, p_up from 54 to 53, because the peer group sold its RevPAR beats and CHH's big moves turn on EPS and guidance.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): reaction-function finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and Street-above-guide finding from -0.5 to -0.4, given 12.8 days to cover.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing EPS estimates ($2.26 / $2.28), so no cap applied.
'What has worked' (a peer print after the company last spoke) kept the read-through positive rather than zero.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus of about $52.7-54.3M needs Q2's $52.9M to repeat, but Q2 included Q1 catch-up. The MRO aviation components segment (APU/landing gear, Piedmont) did $27.7M in Q2 (+38.5% YoY) after only about $16.9M in Q1, which was down YoY on supply-chain timing. H1 revenue grew only 10.4% (avg $47.0M/quarter), and Q3 2025 x 1.104 = $51.0M, about 3-6% below the bar. Backlog rose to about $615M from $580M and management claimed 'excellent revenue visibility', which supports Q3 holding near Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed release dates and Yahoo closes. Q2 2026 (2026-08-05 bmo) revenue $52.9M vs about $44.9M consensus, a +18% beat: +2.3% on the day, then -6.4% the next. Q1 2026 (2026-05-20 bmo) revenue $41.1M vs $40.2M, a small beat from a $32.7 low: +21.0%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-18) on supply-chain and FX worries: -7.5% on the day and -16.3% the next. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12 amc): about +6% after hours, -0.7% close to close. Q2 2025 (2025-08-12): -12.4%. Revenue disappointments are punished, beats are sold or faded.

findings.finding: The EPS bar ($0.38-0.43) sits above Q2's own adjusted EPS of $0.35 (adjusted net income $4.66M) on similar revenue. Q2 R&D rose 122.9% YoY and G&A 16.8%. Gross margin fell in OEM heat transfer (30.1% to 25.9%) and jet engine overhaul (51.9% to 32.0%), offset by MRO aviation components (16.5% to 23.0%). Meeting the EPS bar needs a margin step-up the Q2 cost trend does not show. Cap: the EPS basis is disputed (one aggregator lists Q1 'adjusted EPS 35c' while GAAP diluted EPS was $0.26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS $0.35 vs $0.32 was a narrow beat next to the large revenue beat, and the stock gave back 6.4% the day after the print. Q3 2025 EPS $0.37 vs $0.40, a miss: -0.7% close to close after an after-hours pop.

findings.finding: Honeywell Aerospace's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-28) shows commercial aftermarket sales +2% organic, 'limited by mechanical component availability' from a small number of pacing suppliers. TAT's APU MRO (Honeywell 131-9 and 331 platforms) relies on Honeywell parts, and TAT's Q1 2026 shortfall was blamed on APU component supply disruption. Honeywell also cited 'encouraging signs from pacing suppliers'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 supply-chain shortfall (revenue down YoY) still produced +21% from a depressed price. The Q4 2025 print, when renewed supply disruption was flagged, fell 7.5% then 16.3%.

findings.finding: AAR's fiscal Q1 2027 (June-August 2026, reported 2026-09-28) grew sales 24% to $918M, with Repair, Engineering & Software +31% and Parts Supply +31%, and guided next-quarter growth ex-legacy to 14-16%. This points to strong component MRO and parts demand overlapping two of TAT's three Q3 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TAT's demand-driven revenue beat in Q2 2026 (+18% vs consensus) bought only +2.3% and then faded, so a demand read-through pays little.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day (2026-07-14) moved +4.56%. It has not yet appeared in a reported quarter.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 operating cash flow was -$0.6M (vs +$6.9M in Q2 2025), driven by an $8.3M receivables build and a $3.5M inventory build. Inventory reached $85.2M against $75.5M at year-end. Q3 cash conversion is a quality-of-beat line: a reversal would support the print, a further build would undercut it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's negative cash flow came with the +2.3% / -6.4% fade after a large beat.
